news.title: Open Enrollment Scams Are Here — Don't Click That Link
news.excerpt: Open enrollment season runs through January 15, 2027, and scammers are flooding inboxes and phones with fake health insurance offers. The FCC warns that robocalls and texts pretending to be from "Medicare," "your insurance provider," or "Healthcare.gov" spike during this window. They pressure you to "verify" your Social Security number or pay a fee to keep coverage. Real insurers and government agencies never ask for payment or personal info over an unsolicited call or text. What to do: Hang up. Delete the text. If you need to check your coverage, go directly to Healthcare.gov or call the number on your insurance card. Never use a number or link from the message. Source: FCC.gov — November 1, 2026

news.title: Fake Free Software Downloads Hide Password-Stealing Malware — Microsoft Warns
news.excerpt: That "Free" Download Is a Trap. You search for a cracked version of a paid program, a free game, or a tool to activate Windows. The first result promises exactly what you want. You download it, run the installer, and click through. Behind the scenes, that installer silently adds unwanted programs — some route your traffic through your computer, others enroll you in distributed computing, and some steal browser passwords. Microsoft warned Nov 3: a campaign uses trojanized installers to deliver monetization payloads. What to do: Never download "cracked" software, activators, or free versions of paid programs. Get software only from the official website or Microsoft Store. If you ran a suspicious installer, run a full scan with Windows Security (built in, free) and change browser passwords.

news.title: Big Security Updates Today — Microsoft, Google & Apple Released Patches
news.excerpt:
BIG UPDATE DAY: Microsoft, Google, and Apple released important security updates TODAY to protect your computer from real threats.

Microsoft just released patches for Windows and Office — these fix problems that could let hackers cause trouble. Google added a new scam protection to Chrome. Apple fixed issues on iPhone and Mac.

What to do: Turn on automatic updates and let them run overnight. You don't have to do anything special. Most updates install while you sleep.

Why it matters: Hackers target computers that haven't been updated. Updates close the doors they try to open.

news.title: Fake Windows 11 24H2 Update Scam Steals Data — Patch Tuesday Tomorrow
news.excerpt: A convincing fake Windows 11 24H2 update page is circulating. It mimics a Microsoft support site, uses a believable cumulative-update name, and offers a blue download button for an 83 MB installer. The file is a malicious MSI built with legitimate tools that hides an infostealer

news.title: ClickFix fake browser updates are tricking people into running malware — close the tab
news.excerpt: That "Update Chrome" or "Update Firefox" page that pops up while you're browsing? It's a lie. ClickFix scams mimic real browser updates to get you to copy-paste a malicious command into your terminal. Real browsers update themselves automatically — they never ask you to run commands. Close the tab. If it won't close, hold your power button for 15 seconds until the screen goes black, then turn it back on.

news.title: Scammers Are Faking Official-Looking Notices — Here's the Tell
news.excerpt:
Scammers Are Faking Official-Looking Notices — Here's the Tell.

You get an email or see a webpage that looks exactly like it's from
your bank, the IRS, or a government agency. The logo is perfect.
The formatting is perfect. It says "Immediate action required" and
threatens account closure, legal trouble, or lost benefits if you
don't respond today.

The giveaway: they ask for something no legitimate organization
would ever request by email. Your Social Security number. Your
bank login. A payment in gift cards or wire transfer. Remote access
to your computer.

Real banks and government agencies don't operate this way. They
already have your information. They don't threaten instant disaster.
They don't demand gift cards.

What to do: Don't click any links in the message. Don't call...

posts.title: Firefox 160 Stable Released with Mailto Blocking, PiP Speed Controls, and MKV Support — Free at firefox.com
posts.summary: Firefox 160 stable was released on November 10, 2026, adding the ability to block websites from repeatedly asking to handle mailto: email links, playback speed controls (0.25x to 2.0x) in the Picture-in-Picture video player, support for Matroska (MKV) files with FLAC, MP3, or PCM audio, and a Mini Window feature for keeping tabs always on top. Update free at firefox.com or through Firefox's built-in updater.
posts.truth: Most people don't realize their browser is the first line of defense. Firefox keeps adding privacy features that actually matter — blocking sites from hijacking your email links is a perfect example. Chrome still lets sites spam that prompt.

posts.title: Test Suspicious Files Safely in Windows Sandbox — Free Disposable PC Built Into Windows 11 Pro
posts.summary: Windows Sandbox gives you a lightweight disposable Windows environment to test untrusted apps, open suspicious email attachments, or visit questionable websites without risking your main system. It resets to a clean state every time you close it. Enable it in Windows 11 Pro/Enterprise via Settings > Apps > Optional features > More Windows features > Windows Sandbox, or run 'OptionalFeatures' and check the box.
posts.truth: People click things they shouldn't. A sandbox lets them click safely. I've had customers open "invoice.pdf.exe" in the sandbox — malware runs, sandbox closes, main system stays clean. It's the closest thing to a "delete button" for bad decisions.

posts.title: Microsoft November Patch Tuesday Fixes 1,235 Flaws Including Actively Exploited Outlook Zero-Day
posts.summary: Microsoft's November Patch Tuesday addresses 1,235 security vulnerabilities, including one actively exploited zero-day in Outlook that steals login credentials when a malicious file is opened. The update also includes fixes for Windows, Office, and Edge. Update now via Settings > Windows Update.
posts.truth: Browser and OS exploits are the number one way malware gets in. The Outlook zero-day means just opening a malicious file can steal credentials — no click needed. This is why automatic updates matter: you don't want to be the one who opened that file before patching.

posts.title: Windows 11 November Update Adds Cloud Rebuild Recovery and Redesigned Right-Click Menus
posts.summary: Windows 11 November update adds Cloud Rebuild recovery, redesigned right-click menus, and fixes for Remote Desktop and printing. Rollout is gradual — check Settings > Windows Update to see if it's available for your device.
posts.truth: Cloud Rebuild is a big deal — it lets you reinstall Windows from the cloud without a USB stick, keeping your files. The right-click menu finally gets the classic options back without the extra "Show more options" click. Worth checking for.

posts.title: Restart Once a Week to Clear Memory Leaks and Stuck Updates
posts.summary: Hold your power button for 15 seconds until the screen goes black, wait a moment, then turn it back on. This clears memory leaks, stuck updates, and sluggish performance. Do it every Friday and your computer will stay snappy.
posts.truth: I see computers that haven't been restarted in weeks — they're slow, updates are stuck, and memory is full of leaks. A full power-cycle (hold 15 seconds) clears it all. Do it Friday, start fresh Monday.

posts.title: Microsoft Edge 157 Security Update Fixes Chromium Vulnerabilities — Update at edge://settings/help
posts.summary: Microsoft Edge 157 was released November 5 2026 as the Stable channel main release incorporating the latest Chromium security fixes. Update free by going to edge://settings/help or Settings > About Microsoft Edge. Automatic updates also apply if enabled.
posts.truth: Edge updates silently in the background for most people but I still see machines weeks behind on browser patches. Browser exploits are the number one way malware gets in — a single compromised website can hit an unpatched browser. Taking ten seconds to verify you're current is the highest-ROI security habit there is.

posts.title: Microsoft Fixes Windows 11 Black Screen After Sign In — KB5127648 Resolves Explorer Crash
posts.summary: Microsoft resolved a known issue where some Windows 11 devices show a black screen or fail to load the desktop after sign in caused by an Explorer crash. The fix is included in KB5127648 released October 13 2026 and all later cumulative updates. Install the latest Windows Update at Settings > Windows Update to get the fix.
posts.truth: This black screen bug scared a lot of customers — they thought their computer died. It's just Explorer crashing before the desktop loads. The fix has been out since mid-October but plenty of machines still haven't pulled it. If your screen goes black after login, you're not broken — you're just behind on updates.

posts.title: Firefox 160 Adds On-Device Speech Recognition in 40 Languages — Free Update at firefox.com
posts.summary: Firefox 160 was released November 10 2026 and includes on-device speech recognition using the Web Speech API for real-time speech-to-text conversion in 40 languages. Works on desktop offline with no cloud processing. Update free at firefox.com or open Settings > About Firefox to check for updates.
posts.truth: Most people don't realize their browser can now do speech-to-text locally without sending audio to Google or Microsoft. This is a genuine privacy win — your voice stays on your machine. I've been testing it and it's surprisingly accurate for dictating emails and documents.

posts.title: Chrome 157 Security Update Fixes 213 Bugs Including 7 Critical — Update at chrome://settings/help
posts.summary: Chrome 157 patches 213 security holes including seven critical flaws in graphics, memory handling, and browser features. Update now at chrome://settings/help — it takes two minutes and protects against memory corruption and graphics exploits.

posts.title: Microsoft Released Security Updates for Windows and Office Today — Here's What Changed for You
posts.summary: Microsoft released its monthly security updates for Windows 11, Windows 10, Office, and Edge today. These updates fix problems that could let hackers cause trouble. Let the update run overnight and restart when asked.
posts.truth: Updates are your computer's seatbelt. Skipping them leaves you unprotected.

posts.title: Windows 11 Built-In Troubleshooters Fix Common Problems Automatically — No Download Needed
posts.summary: Windows 11 includes free built-in troubleshooters that automatically diagnose and fix common problems like internet connections audio Windows Update printer issues and more. Run them at Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters. Select the troubleshooter for your issue and click Run.
posts.truth: People call for help with Wi-Fi that won't connect audio that's gone silent or updates that stall — and half the time the built-in troubleshooter fixes it before I even get to the machine. These tools have gotten genuinely good. They're not a magic wand but they're always worth trying first.

posts.title: DAILY BRIEF — Chrome 157 Patches 213 Flaws, CISA Flags SonicWall/Apple/WordPress
posts.summary: Chrome 157 fixes 213 security bugs including 7 critical — update at chrome://settings/help. CISA confirms three new actively exploited flaws: SonicWall SSLVPN, Apple authentication, WordPress core. Patch affected systems immediately.
